headline: Federal safety oversight of MBTA ends after years-long review
dek: The Federal Transit Administration closed its safety management inspection and transferred direct oversight of the Massachusetts system back to the state Department of Public Utilities.
body: The Federal Transit Administration has closed its safety management inspection of the Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities' oversight of the MBTA, state officials said Friday. The move transfers direct federal oversight that began in 2022 back to the DPU.

The inspection followed years of federal concern about the transit system's safety practices. The Healey administration and MBTA said the closure reflects progress on corrective action plans, workforce changes and infrastructure investment, while acknowledging that the system still has work ahead.

DPU Commissioner Staci Rubin said the agency had strengthened its rail-safety staff, technical expertise and oversight processes. MBTA General Manager Phillip Eng said 99% of the system's corrective action plans had been submitted, according to the state and the transit authority.

The MBTA remains under state oversight as it continues track, signal, vehicle and accessibility projects across the region. The federal action marks a change in supervision, not the end of safety monitoring.
author: NorthEast News Desk
